deckTitle: Intensive Care Medicine: The Vital Vigil

cards.power: The Wet-Lung-Wallop. Axe floods the alveoli with protein-rich Sludge, turning the lungs into stiff, unexpandable Stone.
cards.lore: Cytokine-driven damage to the alveolar-capillary barrier creates Baby Lungs—small patches of functional tissue in a sea of collapse.
cards.gradeReason: Alveolar-Axe is a threat image but still condition-first, not role-first.
cards.artworkPrompt: Angry beaver with stone axe smashing glowing lung tissue. Style: watercolor ink sketchbook. Mood: destructive.

cards.power: The Balloon-Support. Keeps the tiny Alveolar-Balloons from snapping shut at the end of every breath.
cards.lore: Increases Functional Residual Capacity. Caveat: Too much PEEP crushes the Heart-Pump (Decreases Preload).
cards.gradeReason: Prop/Balloon-Support is tactically clear; caveat adds depth but the name needs table context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Hedgehog family propping open pink alveoli balloons from inside. Style: watercolor ink. Mood: supportive tension.

cards.power: The Over-Stretch. Pushes too much air into too little lung, tearing the tissue apart.
cards.lore: Volutrauma and Barotrauma. Turns Protective-Ventilation into a destructive Air-Hammer.
cards.gradeReason: Vandal = pure villain embodiment. Air-Hammer destroys from the moment you read it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Gorilla smashing oversized balloon lung with ventilator hose, sparks flying. Style: ink sketchbook. Mood: violent destruction.

cards.power: The Gravity-Flip. Let the Back-Lungs breathe while the Front-Lungs rest.
cards.lore: Homogenizes stress and strain. Moves the weight of the heart and gut off the dorsal alveoli to improve the Ventilation-Perfusion-Match.
cards.gradeReason: Gravity-Flip is an instant stage direction. Pivot tells you exactly the move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Badgers hauling large walrus with pulley system onto its front. Style: watercolor. Mood: cooperative, purposeful.

cards.power: The Pressure-Anchor. Clamps the leaky Peripheral-Pipes to ensure the Brain-and-Heart-Vaults stay pressurized.
cards.lore: The Vasopressor of Choice. Increases MAP without over-revving the heart-engine.
cards.gradeReason: North Star + Pressure-Anchor = first-line commander. Own the role from the name alone.
cards.artworkPrompt: Starry owl clamping glowing blood vessel branches, compass north overlay. Style: ink watercolor. Mood: authoritative calm.

cards.power: The Piston-Push. Screams at the failing heart-engine to squeeze harder.
cards.lore: Used in Cardiogenic-Carl. Caveat: It's a vasodilator—he might drop the MAP while boosting the flow.
cards.gradeReason: Dynamo + Piston-Push = you are the heart-screamer. Pure immediate embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cheetah with jet turbine strapped to chest pushing glowing heart to explode. Style: ink watercolor. Mood: overdrive.

cards.power: The Real-Time-Radar. Gives the Beat-by-Beat truth, spotting every Pulse-Pressure-Variation.
cards.lore: Allows for frequent blood gases. If the waveform Dampens, the Archer is hitting a wall or pipes are kinked.
cards.gradeReason: Archer = perpetual watcher. Real-Time-Radar is zero-lag clarity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Armored falcon archer drawing bow at red ECG waveform target. Style: ink sketchbook. Mood: precise vigilance.

cards.power: The Deep-Diver. Swims through the heart into the lungs to see the pressure in the Left-Atrium-Lobby.
cards.lore: Differentiates Heart-Failure-Flood from Sepsis-Leak. Rare now, but essential for Complex-Congestion.
cards.gradeReason: Deep-Diver is evocative but 'Rare now' reads as a disclaimer, dampening the embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Sleek eel navigating maze inside anatomical heart toward glowing left atrium chamber. Style: ink. Mood: precise navigation.

cards.power: The 24-Hour-Sieve. Slowly cleans the blood, removing Toxin-Tokens without crashing the blood pressure.
cards.lore: Gentle. Mimics the natural kidney for wrestlers who are too unstable for a fast Flush.
cards.gradeReason: 24-Hour-Sieve is functional and accurate but the card is primarily a machine description.
cards.artworkPrompt: Glowing water dam with slow steady filtration into ICU bed. Style: watercolor. Mood: relentless slow work.

cards.power: The Electrical-Eraser. Shorts out the heart's wiring, leading to the Sine-Wave-Silence.
cards.lore: Stops the resting membrane potential. Treat with Calcium-the-Shield to protect wires, then Insulin-the-Evictor.
cards.gradeReason: Killer + Electrical-Eraser = zero ambiguity. You are the electrolyte assassin.
cards.artworkPrompt: Jellyfish army electrocuting anatomical heart with flat ECG Sine-Wave outcome. Style: ink watercolor. Mood: deadly electric.

cards.power: The Protein-Melter. Turns the blood sour, causing Pressor-Pumps to stop and the heart to stumble.
cards.lore: A sign of Tissue-Starvation. If the cells can't breathe, they vomit acid. A signal of Energy-Failure.
cards.gradeReason: Abyss = environment of doom. 'Cells vomit acid' is viscerally G1 performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Armored rhino warrior dissolving in green acid swamp, toxic vapor rising. Style: ink sketchbook. Mood: corrosive despair.

cards.power: The Machine-Shield. Eats the calcium in the dialysis circuit so blood doesn't Clot-the-Filter.
cards.lore: Regional means it only works inside the machine. Caveat: If the liver can't process it, causes Calcium-Crashing.
cards.gradeReason: Machine-Shield is functional but reads as a mechanism description more than a role invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Armadillo blocking calcium crystals from entering dialysis machine gears. Style: watercolor ink. Mood: protective mechanical.

cards.power: The Capillary-Collapse. Opens all Volume-Valves and turns vessel-walls into Leaky-Cheese.
cards.lore: Immune-overdrive causes massive vasodilation. Blood hides in Peripheral-Puddles, leaving the brain dry.
cards.gradeReason: Sam = character. Leaky-Cheese is disgustingly perfect. Blood hiding in Puddles is pure embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Flame-armored lizard monster spraying fire at leaky blood vessel walls. Style: watercolor. Mood: catastrophic riot.

cards.power: The Bacterial-Beacon. Glows bright when Bacterial-Punks are in the blood, dim for Viral-Vandals.
cards.lore: Guides when to start—and when to stop—the Antibiotic-Artillery.
cards.gradeReason: Bacterial-Beacon is clear but the card's role is information delivery, not performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Green glowing fly on radar screen surrounded by dark bug silhouettes. Style: ink sketchbook. Mood: biosurveillance.

cards.power: The Hypoxia-Tax. Represents the Oxygen-Debt from failing aerobic metabolism.
cards.lore: High Lactate = Tissue Ischemia. Clearing the Lactate proves the Resuscitation-Rescue is winning.
cards.gradeReason: Debt-Collector + Hypoxia-Tax = crime metaphor that clicks instantly. Fully embodiable villain.
cards.artworkPrompt: Vampire bat with money bag chasing bear through red blood cells. Style: watercolor ink. Mood: relentless debt pursuit.

cards.power: The Root-Removal. Knows that Antibiotic-Ammo fails if the Nest isn't destroyed.
cards.lore: Ubi pus, ibi evacua. (If there is pus, drain it). If the line is dirty, pull it.
cards.gradeReason: Striker + Root-Removal + Latin war cry. This card wants to be screamed at a table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Lion warrior in cape slashing open green infected nest with flaming sword. Style: watercolor. Mood: decisive conquest.

cards.power: The Skull-Squeeze. Swelling brain crushes the Oxygen-Entry-Vessels.
cards.lore: The skull is a Closed-Box. If ICP reaches MAP, the Brain-Death-Bell rings.
cards.gradeReason: Skull-Squeeze is visceral but the card name leads with a clinical abbreviation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Brain in steel vice with ECG flatline warning lights, skull as closed metal box. Style: ink. Mood: pressure crisis.

cards.power: The Water-Sucker. Pulls water out of swollen brain-tissue and into the blood.
cards.lore: Creates an Osmotic-Gradient. Caveat: Mannitol causes Diuresis-Drain, 3% Saline keeps volume in pipes.
cards.gradeReason: Name is redundant (Osmotic-the-Osmotic). Water-Sucker is fine but no character to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Crab knight in helmet drinking water from swollen brain with long straw. Style: ink watercolor. Mood: clinical extraction.

cards.power: The Mainframe-Mute. Puts the brain to sleep and lowers the Oxygen-Burn-Rate.
cards.lore: Allows the Daily-Wake-Up-Test. Caveat: PRIS (Infusion Syndrome) causes acidosis and heart failure.
cards.gradeReason: 'Milk' is a perfect nickname. Mainframe-Mute is the best sedation power in any deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Fluffy white sheep exhaling sleep cloud through medical vial into patient brain. Style: watercolor. Mood: dreamy descent.

cards.power: The Conscious-Calm. Provides Analgo-Sedation—sleepy but can answer the Neuro-Check.
cards.lore: Doesn't stop the breathing-drive. Great for Ventilator-Weaning. Caveat: Can cause Brady-Bill (Slow heart).
cards.gradeReason: Conscious-Calm is a clear state but 'Precedex' is brand jargon that breaks immersion.
cards.artworkPrompt: Sloth hanging from IV drip monitor in hospital glow, relaxed but eyes open. Style: watercolor. Mood: alert sedation.

cards.power: The Vein-Feed. Bypasses the Gut-Gate to feed directly through the blood.
cards.lore: The Last Resort. TPN loves the Liver-Limp and Line-Infection-Iggies. If the gut works, use the gut!
cards.gradeReason: Typo ('Parental' for 'Parenteral') undermines credibility. LORE tone is lecture not invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Hummingbird injecting nutrients directly into vein swirl bypassing intestinal tunnel. Style: watercolor. Mood: emergency feeding.

cards.power: The Acid-Erosion. Eats the stomach lining during the Stress-Storm, causing a Hidden-Bleed.
cards.lore: Prevented by PPI-the-Lock or H2-the-Hinderer.
cards.gradeReason: Shadow and Hidden-Bleed are evocative but the card name is descriptive rather than character-driven.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dark shadow rat gnawing stomach wall in secret, acid dripping from teeth. Style: ink. Mood: hidden erosion.

cards.power: The Static-Snake. Intestines stop moving, causing Belly-Bloat and Vomitus-Vex.
cards.lore: Often caused by Opioid-Overload or Electrolyte-Emptying.
cards.gradeReason: Idle + ON STRIKE! sign on the snake is pure theater. The labor metaphor clicks immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Pink intestine snake on velvet pillow holding ON STRIKE placard, completely inert. Style: ink. Mood: lazy protest.

cards.power: The Detox-Failure. Stops cleaning the blood, letting Ammonia-the-Fog cloud the brain.
cards.lore: Watch for Cerebral-Edema-Swelling. It is a race for the Transplant-Train.
cards.gradeReason: Limp says everything in one word. Race for the Transplant-Train has genuine urgency.
cards.artworkPrompt: Opossum at rusted closed factory CLOSED sign, ammonia clouds rising over city. Style: ink watercolor. Mood: shutdown dread.

cards.power: The Clot-and-Bleed. Uses up all Clot-Tokens in tiny, useless fights, leaving nothing for Major-Leaks.
cards.lore: A Consumption-Coagulopathy. Treat the underlying Sam-Sepsis to stop the spiral.
cards.gradeReason: Clot-and-Bleed captures the paradox well but DIC acronym-first creates distance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Porcupine bleeding from quill punctures while uselessly clotting small wounds everywhere. Style: ink. Mood: futile crisis.

cards.power: The Hole-Stoppage. The first line of defense against Capillary-Leaks.
cards.lore: In the ICU, Plugs get eaten by Sam-Sepsis and Spleen-the-Sponge.
cards.gradeReason: Plug = function = embodiment in one word. You know exactly what you do.
cards.artworkPrompt: Golden retriever puppies stacking golden bricks to plug cracking wall leaks. Style: watercolor. Mood: cooperative defense.

cards.power: The Liquid-Gold. Restores the Coagulation-Cascade when the INR-Alarm is ringing.
cards.lore: Essential for Warf-Reversal and Massive-Hemorrhage.
cards.gradeReason: Liquid-Gold is great. FFP acronym-first is the barrier to full G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Golden liquid poured into rusted clock gears restoring cascading mechanism. Style: ink watercolor. Mood: restoration.

cards.power: The Real-Time-Clot-Movie. Tells exactly why blood isn't clotting: Factor-Failure, Platelet-Paucity, or Fibrin-Frenzy?
cards.lore: Guided Goal-Directed-Therapy. Don't guess—TEG it!
cards.gradeReason: Thromboelastography as a card name is impossible to embody. Six-syllable subtitle kills the invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Tech spider weaving glowing red diagnostic web with real-time clotting pattern data. Style: ink. Mood: precision analysis.

cards.power: The Vessel-Sensitizer. Helps the Norad-Pressor work better by making vessels sensitive to the signal.
cards.lore: Replaces Relative-Adrenal-Insufficiency.
cards.gradeReason: Vessel-Sensitizer is clear but the compound name is a descriptor not an invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Meerkat fixing broken radio dish antenna to receive norad signal better. Style: ink sketchbook. Mood: signal restoration.

cards.power: The Calcium-Cutter. Stops the Muscle-Meltdown in Malignant Hyperthermia.
cards.lore: Prevents the runaway release of calcium from the Sarcoplasmis-Silo.
cards.gradeReason: Inferno-Cooler and the penguin firefighter are G1 visually, but the drug name leads.
cards.artworkPrompt: Penguin firefighter in full gear hosing flaming engine block muscle with ice water. Style: ink. Mood: emergency cooldown.

cards.power: The Muscle-Wake-Up. Grabs Paralyzer-Punks and drags them away from the Nerve-Junction.
cards.lore: Immediate reversal of neuromuscular blockade. No Wet-Side-Effects like Neostigmine.
cards.gradeReason: Reverser + Muscle-Wake-Up. You know the role in three words. Best power in the anesthesia section.
cards.artworkPrompt: Anteater with vacuum backpack dragging paralysis monsters away from glowing nerve synapse. Style: ink. Mood: decisive rescue.

cards.power: The Surgical-Calm. The go-to for continuous Analgesia-Infusion in the ventilated wrestler.
cards.lore: Rapid on/off. Caveat: Causes Chest-Wall-Rigidity-Stiff if pushed too fast.
cards.gradeReason: Surgical-Calm is precise but 'Fast-Acting' is a product description, not a character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dark purple panther running through barbed wire in slow motion, pain dissolving. Style: watercolor. Mood: swift analgesic silence.

cards.power: The Physiological-Fill. The Gold Standard for filling the Septic-Tank.
cards.lore: Closer to blood than Normal-Saline-the-Salty, which can cause Chloride-Acid-Abyss.
cards.gradeReason: Balanced is a quality not a role. Gold Standard is aspirational but not performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Green frog hugging electrolyte-filled crystalloid bottle with rainbow colored ions inside. Style: watercolor. Mood: equilibrium.

cards.power: The Water-Magnet. Stays in the Pipe-Highway and pulls fluid out of the Tissue-Swamps (Edema).
cards.lore: Used when crystalloids fail or after large-volume Ascites-Draining.
cards.gradeReason: Water-Magnet is a great power. 'The-Colloid' is categorical, not a name to inhabit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Pelican with giant magnet pulling fluid drops from swampy tissue back into vessel. Style: watercolor. Mood: oncotic pull.

cards.power: The Squeeze-Out. Removes the Extra-Weight post-shock to let the lungs breathe.
cards.lore: Lavitra-the-Lasix is the main tool. Being Too-Wet increases the Ventilator-Time.
cards.gradeReason: Dry-Down + Squeeze-Out = you know the move the moment you read it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Camel squeezing giant sponge dry over drain bucket, lungs visible expanding behind. Style: ink. Mood: deliberate drying.

cards.power: The Fluid-Challenge-Without-Fluid. Tells if the heart wants more volume before you pour it in.
cards.lore: The Reversible-Auto-Transfusion. If MAP goes up, the heart is Fluid-Responsive.
cards.gradeReason: Fluid-Challenge-Without-Fluid is clever but the meta-concept needs explanation at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Kangaroo doctor lifting hippo patient legs at 45 degrees while reading heart monitor. Style: watercolor. Mood: diagnostic lift.

cards.power: The Emergency-Return. When the Golden-Tube is removed too early and the Airway-Assassins return.
cards.lore: High-risk move. Swelling (Edema) makes the second pass much harder than the first.
cards.gradeReason: Panic says everything. Airway-Assassins return = immediate dramatic stakes at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Octopus emerging from dark tunnel grabbing back airway tube from fleeing doctor. Style: ink. Mood: alarming emergency.

cards.power: The Machine-Induced-Crush. The ventilator Pops a lung-bleb, squashing the heart.
cards.lore: Always disconnect the vent first in sudden PEA to rule out Auto-PEEP or Tension-Tony.
cards.gradeReason: Tony is a character. 'Disconnect the vent first' is a stage direction you can shout.
cards.artworkPrompt: Mechanical elephant inflating balloon that crushes anatomical heart against stone wall. Style: ink. Mood: machine catastrophe.

cards.power: The Clot-Irony. Makes platelets clump together while numbers drop, causing Venous-and-Arterial-Jams.
cards.lore: Immune-mediated riot. Stop Heparin immediately and use Argatroban-the-Alternative.
cards.gradeReason: Hunter + Clot-Irony perfectly captures the paradox. The irony IS the embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Fox archer shooting golden treasure bars while platelet counter falls. Style: watercolor ink. Mood: paradox trap.

cards.power: The Highway-Block. A clot-monster from the Leg-Deep-Veins jams the Lung-Entrance.
cards.lore: In the ICU, the Phantom is often completely silent until it is too late.
cards.gradeReason: Phantom = invisible killer. 'Completely silent until too late' is the most chilling lore in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dark shark-monster clot surging from veins to block glowing pink lung gateway. Style: ink. Mood: silent deadly arrival.

cards.power: The Machine-Breach. Bacterial-Punks crawl down the Golden-Tube to start a riot.
cards.lore: Prevented by Head-Up-Position and Oral-Chlorhexidine-Chloe.
cards.gradeReason: Machine-Breach and Bacterial-Punks are vivid but VAP acronym-first creates clinical distance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Green bacteria monsters crawling through ventilator tube into pink lung tissue party. Style: ink. Mood: invasion riot.

cards.power: The IV-Invasion. Staph-the-Skin-Steward enters the Blood-Highway through the CVC-Portal.
cards.lore: Scrub the Hub! If the line is infected, it must be Evicted.
cards.gradeReason: IV-Invasion is solid. 'Scrub the Hub!' is memorable but the six-letter acronym leads.
cards.artworkPrompt: Crowned slug entering glowing blue central line portal into blood highway. Style: ink sketchbook. Mood: stealthy infiltration.

cards.power: The Gut-Explosion. Takes over the Bowel-Basement after Antibiotic-Artillery kills the good guards.
cards.lore: Smells like a Horse-Barn. Treat with Vancomy-the-Vault (Oral).
cards.gradeReason: 'Smells like a Horse-Barn' is G1 gold. Gut-Explosion needs no explanation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Crowned skunk villain in green cloak taking over intestine tunnel with ON STRIKE flag. Style: ink. Mood: foul takeover.

cards.power: The Armor-Plated-Punks. Multidrug-Resistance shields laugh at standard Antibiotic-Ammo.
cards.lore: They use Efflux-Pumps and Enzyme-Blasters (Carbapenemases) to survive.
cards.gradeReason: Superbugs + Armor-Plated-Punks = you are the invincible army. No context needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Squad of armored turtle-soldiers with antibiotic syringes bouncing off their shields. Style: ink. Mood: invincible squad.

cards.power: The Test-Drive. The machine steps back, letting the wrestler breathe alone for 30-120 mins.
cards.lore: Passes if the Heart-Rate and Work-of-Breathing remain stable and low.
cards.gradeReason: Wrestler is the whole deck's frame character. Test-Drive is a perfect clinical-to-game translation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Mechanical bird skeleton trying first solo flight while ventilator steps back watching. Style: pencil sketch. Mood: hopeful trial.

cards.power: The Hallucination-Haze. Makes the wrestler see Shadow-Monsters and pull at their tubes.
cards.lore: Caused by Sleep-Sabotage, Benzodiazepine-Bouncers, and Sam-Sepsis.
cards.gradeReason: Daze + Hallucination-Haze + Shadow-Monsters. You are the ICU nightmare. Pure embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Chameleon surrounded by dark shadow monsters in purple haze pulling at IV tubes. Style: watercolor ink. Mood: delirious terror.

cards.power: The Long-Shadow. The wrestler remains weak and forgetful for months after leaving the Vital-Vigil.
cards.lore: ICU-Acquired-Weakness. The muscles melted away during the long sleep.
cards.gradeReason: Long-Shadow is poignant but the Post-ICU-Struggle subtitle is descriptive, not inviting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Old tortoise with walking cane leaving neon hospital behind, long shadow stretching forward. Style: watercolor. Mood: slow recovery.

cards.power: The Peaceful-Exit. When the Scrimmage is lost, focus shifts to a Quiet-Mat without pain.
cards.lore: Withdrawal of Life-Sustaining Treatment. Morphine and Midazolam ensure the final breath is soft.
cards.gradeReason: The most emotionally immediate card in the deck. 'Final breath is soft' lands without a second of confusion.
cards.artworkPrompt: White swan gliding on still dark water with soft gold sunrise, IV line trailing behind. Style: watercolor. Mood: peaceful release.

cards.power: The Main-Line. Allows for Pressor-Pumps, TPN-Feeding, and Fast-Fluid-Filling.
cards.lore: Allows CVP monitoring. Caveat: Watch for Pneumo-the-Puncture during placement.
cards.gradeReason: Cavalry is a strong metaphor but the LORE warning note shifts tone to cautionary.
cards.artworkPrompt: Mechanical squid torpedo with three tubes charging through blue bloodstream. Style: ink. Mood: armed arrival.

cards.power: The Organ-Perfusion-Monitor. Tells the surgeon if Kidney-Filters are getting enough blood.
cards.lore: Oliguria-the-Small-Flow is the very first sign of Shock-Sam.
cards.gradeReason: Sentry is a clear role but the monitoring function describes rather than invites.
cards.artworkPrompt: Royal guard duck in uniform watching empty drain pool for urine output signals. Style: ink. Mood: vigilant monitoring.

cards.power: The Panic-Drain. When the body's filters fail completely and the AEIOU-Alarms ring.
cards.lore: High potassium or pulmonary edema that won't respond to Lasix requires the machine NOW.
cards.gradeReason: Disaster + Panic-Drain + AEIOU-Alarms = urgency is instant and total. No ambiguity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Red ape smashing giant AEIOU keyboard buttons in emergency filter meltdown. Style: ink. Mood: alarm chaos.

cards.power: The Ultimate-Bypass. Takes blood outside the body, gasses it with oxygen, and pumps it back.
cards.lore: The Highest-Level-Support. Buys weeks of time for the biological heart or lungs to heal.
cards.gradeReason: Extra-Lung is the most perfectly coined name in the deck. You know exactly what you are.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cybernetic whale with glowing pink lung wings pumping oxygenated blood in underwater circuit. Style: watercolor. Mood: ultimate support.

cards.power: The Meta-Physiologist.
cards.lore: Is the CO2 rising? Is the MAP holding? Is the Lactate clearing? Balance the system! Stay fluffy!
cards.gradeReason: Meta-card that embodifies the conductor of chaos. 'Stay fluffy!' is a perfect FrizzleBob closer.
cards.artworkPrompt: Multi-armed rabbit doctor monitoring six screens simultaneously in glowing ICU control room. Style: ink. Mood: orchestrated multitasking.

cards.power: The Acid-Blockade.
cards.lore: Identify the Sensitivity-Tool to help pressors work (Hydrocort-Support) and the Drain-Tool for the acid (CRRT-the-Constant).
cards.gradeReason: Strong scenario card but requires knowing other cards to play — G2 until context is established.
cards.artworkPrompt: Owl Norad and meerkat Hydrocort fighting green acid wave with CRRT drain machine. Style: ink. Mood: combined effort.

cards.power: The Air-Trap.
cards.lore: Identify the Machine-Induced-Killer (Tension-the-Tony). The very first move: Disconnect the Vent!
cards.gradeReason: 'Disconnect the Vent!' is a stage direction you can shout at the table. Instant performative command.
cards.artworkPrompt: Gorilla and elephant in crisis code, DISCONNECT warning flashing, PEA flatline visible. Style: ink. Mood: code alarm.

cards.power: The Sarcoplasmic-Fire.
cards.lore: Identify the Inland-Inferno (Malignant Hyperthermia) and deploy the Calcium-Cutter (Dantrolene-the-Inferno-Cooler).
cards.gradeReason: Sarcoplasmic-Fire is dramatic but the reference chain reads as a puzzle, not a performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Penguin firefighter hosing flame thermometer inside muscle-fire operating room. Style: ink. Mood: contained emergency.

verdict: The Vital Vigil is the strongest MedKayfab deck to date. The X-the-Y naming system lands with almost metronomic consistency, and the Quest cards are a genuine design innovation — clinical reasoning scenarios that make cards talk to each other. Three cards drag it back from a 10: Osmotic-the-Osmotic (redundant name), TPN-the-Total-Parental (typo erodes trust), and TEG-the-Thromboelastography (unpronounceable). Comfort-Care-the-Transition is the most emotionally resonant card in the entire MedKayfab canon. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: 56 ICU battle cards — from Septic-Sam to Comfort-Care-the-Transition — that turn intensive care medicine into a wrestling match you can actually survive. For nurses, residents, and anyone who spends nights in the Vital Vigil.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — FrizzleBob as frantic ICU attending at control panel, glowing lungs on screen, gremlins chewing wires.
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'Intensive Care Medicine: The Vital Vigil' — subtitle-first, tagline 'Titrating the threshold between life and the void' is precise and poetic.
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Perfect. The chaotic-but-controlled ICU energy is exactly what the deck delivers.
coverQA.coverOriginality: 5 — ICU control panel + colorful IV lines + gremlins is a completely original composition.
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — Extremely shareable but the illustration is busy at thumbnail scale.
coverQA.coverNote: Best cover in the MedKayfab series so far. The 'Call Doc Frizzle!' and 'KayfaBIZARRO!' callout gremlins add humor without cluttering the core visual. The tagline is strong enough to carry a standalone social post.

notes: 15 pages: 1 cover + 14 card pages x 4 cards = 56 cards. TAPE-01 through TAPE-04 labels appear only on page 2 (respiratory cluster) — design system not extended to other thematic groups. 'The Sabotaged Sketchbook' runs as sub-header from page 3 onward. Pages 13-15 shift to rougher pencil-sketch style (intentional or late additions). Osmotic-the-Osmotic: naming oversight — both halves are identical. TPN-the-Total-Parental: 'Parental' should be 'Parenteral'. CRRT page 4 shows 'ORE:' — 'L' is image-edge cropped, full text reads LORE. Quest cards (page 15) reference specific earlier cards by name creating a unique cross-card dependency system — first seen in MedKayfab series.

urgent: Rename 'Osmotic-the-Osmotic' — redundant name, needs a character noun (e.g. 'Mannitol-the-Brain-Drainer')
quickWins: Add visual indicator or card border color to distinguish Quest cards from standard cards
Extend TAPE label system to other thematic clusters (Sepsis, Neuro, Coagulation)
niceToHave: Add FrizzleBob's Quest 4 covering AKI/oliguria diagnosis chain
Consider companion RULES_as_CARDS page explaining how Quest cards work at the table
